audit_findings.title: Unpaid $26 million judgment may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: In accordance with applicable accounting standards, the Company recorded a litigation related accrual of $ 6,500,000 in the third quarter of 2022 and incremental litigation related accruals of $ 17,200,000 in the first quarter of 2024 and $ 2,300,000 in the second quarter of 2024 when the Amended Corrected Final Judgment was issued, for a total of $ 26,000,000 , as its estimate based on the awarded judgments, including enhanced damages, pre-judgment interest, costs and attorney fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q demonstrates that Vicor paid the full $28.557m judgment, including post-judgment interest, on March 18, 2026. The June 30, 2026 cash balance of $453.582m is after that payment, and accrued litigation was zero. Deducting it again would double count the obligation.
audit_findings.action: Document the March 18 payment and reconcile it to the $28.557m cash-flow adjustment; no valuation rerun is needed.

audit_findings.title: The supplied roll-forward does not prove the $45 million settlement was purged
audit_findings.magnitude: $45.0m receipt and $5.1m related legal fees versus $36.3m OE anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: 2025 OE anchor and consequent operating DCF
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company received a patent litigation settlement payment of $45,000,000 (as described in more detail in Note 16 to the Consolidated Financial Statements).
audit_findings.explanation: This remains an unresolved possibility because no OE roll-forward was supplied. The receipt exceeds the entire anchor, so any retained amount could materially overstate value through capitalization and double counting in cash. Conversely, removing the receipt while retaining the associated $5.1m legal cost would understate normalized OE. The filings establish the amounts but not their treatment in the computed anchor.
audit_findings.action: Produce the complete 2025 OE roll-forward showing separate removal of the $45.0m receipt, normalization of related taxes, and treatment of the $5.1m directly associated legal fees; rerun all scenarios if any inconsistency is found.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 tax profile may not represent sustainable after-tax owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.648m valuation-allowance reversal, $27.197m 2025 deferred-tax benefit, and $4.863m 2025 cash taxes; sustainable valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: after-tax OE anchor and projected OE through the terminal period
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, at December 31, 2025, the Company reversed $ 43,648,000 of its valuation allowance related to certain deductible temporary differences expected to be realized in future periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The deferred-tax reversal is a demonstrated one-time accounting benefit, but whether it entered the OE anchor is unresolved. More importantly, the DCF projects one after-tax OE figure without an explicit transition from currently sheltered cash taxes to normalized taxes. Vicor had $43.081m of federal NOLs and material credits at year-end 2025, but these benefits are finite. Their exhaustion could materially reduce recurring OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to cash taxes, prove exclusion of the deferred-tax benefit, build a year-by-year NOL and credit utilization schedule, and rerun the DCF with normalized federal, state, and foreign cash taxes after the attributes are consumed.

audit_findings.title: A sharp royalty step-up may be embedded as permanent earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $57.384m of 2025 royalty revenue, equal to 158.1% of the $36.3m OE anchor; runoff effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: normalized OE, explicit-period growth, and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: Revenues from licensing arrangements were approximately $57,384,000, $46,595,000, and $15,872,000 in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, representing approximately 14.1%, 13.0%, and 3.9% of total net revenues in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The royalty contribution is presently embedded in reported operations, while the valuation applies company-wide growth rates and no explicit royalty runoff. The filed amount is large relative to the anchor. First-half 2026 royalties of $45.391m and a new license agreement support near-term continuation, but they do not establish duration through the terminal period because license concentration, minimums, termination rights, and covered-patent lives are absent from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the license-level economics and patent-expiration schedule, separate royalty OE from product OE, and rerun bear, base, and bull cases with explicit renewal and runoff assumptions.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash and cash-flow adjustments may include a minority-owned claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.275m June 2026 NCI balance, 0.03% of the $964m base equity value; 2025 NCI income was $0.040m, 0.11% of the $36.3m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: OE attributable to common shareholders and bridge cash attributable to the parent
audit_findings.evidence: Vicor Japan Company, Ltd. (“VJCL”), our 92.5%-owned Japanese subsidiary, which is engaged in sales and customer support activities exclusively for the sale of certain products customized by VJCL for the Japanese market, is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.
audit_findings.explanation: The consolidated-versus-parent mismatch is real in principle, but the filed NCI balance and attributable income establish a very small scale. Even removing the full $0.275m carrying claim would change base value by less than $0.01 per diluted share and cannot affect the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document the NCI allocation in the OE and bridge workpapers; rerun only if subsidiary-level records reveal an attributable amount materially exceeding the filed NCI measures.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may omit an illiquid non-operating security
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.525m filed fair value, approximately $0.052 per diluted share and 0.26% of the $964m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: non-operating asset added in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024 , the Company held one auction rate security with a par value of $ 3,000,000 and an estimated fair value of approximately $ 2,462,000 and $ 2,641,000 , respectively, purchased through and held in custody by a broker-dealer affiliate of Bank of America, N.A., that has experienced failed auctions (the “Failed Auction Security”) since February 2008.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission: the June 2026 filing separately reports the security as a long-term investment, while the bridge includes only cash and short-term investments. Its filed fair value is nevertheless only 0.26% of base equity value, so adding it would not materially change any scenario or the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Add the June 30, 2026 fair value of $2.525m as a separate bridge asset, subject to the chosen illiquidity treatment, and update per-share values for completeness.
